One of Donald Trump’s controversial, taxpayer-funded ads has been given a brutal reworking by a veterans group.

VoteVets, a progressive political action committee representing veterans and military families, spoofed Trump’s “final battle” ad — a clone of a video he’s shared for years and one of three taxpayer-funded spots released ahead of the 2026 midterms that have drawn anger this week.

Trump’s original spot shows him walking down a hallway and saying:

In the VoteVets version, Trump walks down the hallway but with a very different message.

A voice sounding like Trump’s says:

As the parody plays, a Reuters headline flashes onscreen reading: “Trump approval falls to record low of 32% as high costs bite.”

A screenshot from Fox News then appears showing Trump alongside his sons, Eric and Donald Trump Jr., above the caption: “Biggest grift of all time.”

And as the reworked voice-over talks about casting out “the incompetent,” footage of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth comes onscreen.
